facts.statement: The study used a cross-sectional design analyzing MRI scans from 2187 people with multiple sclerosis and normative data.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Gray matter shrinkage was linked to how central a brain region is in functional networks and was limited by both physical and functional brain connections.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Damage to connections caused by lesions and genetic vulnerability had only minor effects on the observed brain atrophy.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study found that network mechanisms drive neurodegeneration in MS and might work differently depending on the specific disease subtype or phase.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The patterns of brain shrinkage were tied to connectivity issues in specific areas including the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortex, as well as the hippocampus, amygdala, and thalamus.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Measuring network connectivity improved the ability to explain how brain atrophy progresses over time in people with MS.
facts.subject: humans
